==Problem==
Joe had walked half way from home to school when he realized he was late. He ran the rest of the way to school. He ran 3 times as fast as he walked. Joe took 6 minutes to walk half way to school. How many minutes did it take Joe to get from home to school?

<math> \textbf{(A)}\ 7\qquad\textbf{(B)}\ 7.3\qquad\textbf{(C)}\ 7.7\qquad\textbf{(D)}\ 8\qquad\textbf{(E)}\ 8.3 </math>

==Solution 1==
We can use the equation <math>d=rt</math> where <math>d</math> is the distance, <math>r</math> is the rate, and <math>t</math> is the time. The distances he ran and walked are equal, so <math>r_rt_r=r_wt_w</math>, where <math>r_r</math> is the rate at which he ran, <math>t_r</math> is the time for which he ran, <math>r_w</math> is the rate at which he walked, and <math>t_w</math> is the time for which he walked. Because he runs three times faster than he walks, <math>r_r=3r_w</math>. We want to find the time he ran, <math>t_r = \frac{r_wt_w}{t_r} = \frac{(r_w)(6)}{3r_w} = 2</math> minutes. He traveled for a total of <math>6+2=\boxed{\textbf{(D)}\ 8}</math> minutes.

==Solution 2== 
We know that it took Joe <imath>6</imath> minutes to walk halfway. If he ran <imath>3</imath> times as fast as that, he went <imath>\frac63 = 2</imath> minutes for the other half (as <imath>t=\frac{d}{s}</imath> and if we multiply <imath>s</imath> by <imath>3</imath> we are essentially dividing <imath>t</imath> by <imath>3</imath>). Therefore, we have <imath>6 + 2 = 8</imath> minutes.

==Solution 3== 
According to <imath>d = rt</imath>, and if we assume the distance from home to school is <imath>1</imath> mile, then <imath>\frac{1}{2} = 6r</imath>, meaning <imath>r = \frac{1}{12}\text{ mph}</imath>. Then, given that he runs <imath>3</imath> times the speed he walks, he runs at <imath>\frac{3}{12}\text{ mph}</imath> or <imath>\frac{1}{4}\text{ mph}</imath>. Also, note that he only has <imath>\frac{1}{2}</imath> mile left to reach school. Therefore, once again using <imath>d = rt</imath>, <imath>\frac{1}{2} = \frac{1}{4}t</imath>, and <imath>t = 2</imath>. Combining the given <imath>6</imath> minutes and the deduced <imath>2</imath> minutes, we reach <imath>\boxed{8\text{ minutes}}</imath>.

-N.
